$comment: Pipeline parameters. Source bindings, thresholds and detection rules live here so the code carries no domain values and no magic numbers. Dimension derivations live in dimensions.json. See docs/CUBE_SCHEMA.md.

snapshot.$comment: A first-registration month is the snapshot month only if it holds at least this share of the median of the months before it (trailing_window_months of them). A few rows dated after the register's own month are then not mistaken for the next snapshot. The lowest real month on record, 2020-04, held 7% of its trailing median (measured on the 2026-10 snapshot).

schedule.$comment: From this day of the month (UTC) a run that builds nothing fails if the previous month's snapshot is still not built (docs/DATA_SOURCES.md, Refresh timing).

hybrid_classification.$comment: mild_hybrid_models.csv: which hybrid nameplates are mild or full. Match columns are the model_registry_conditions above. See docs/METRICS.md for the coverage figure.

registrations_surviving.$pairs_comment: The two-dimensional slices this dataset emits, each [dim_a, dim_b], written to pairs/{dataset}/{dim_a}__{dim_b}.parquet. Only pairs a chart or filter needs (docs/CUBE_SCHEMA.md, Pair slices).
registrations_surviving.$facts_comment: The fact table: counts by month and every dimension listed here, one Parquet file per column under facts/{dataset}/, so the browser can answer any combination by downloading only the columns a question needs (docs/CUBE_SCHEMA.md, Fact table; D-058). region is left out on purpose until the Stage 2 privacy review (D-078): it is where the vehicle's owner lives, and with it two in three of the table's rows counted a single vehicle.

registrations_flow.$comment: Read from the supplied source nzta_dashboard (the `supplied` block), through the same normalise, derive and output code as the register. The same require as registrations_surviving, so the two count the same kinds of vehicle: the dashboard's RE-REG and SCRATCH rows are in the store and are not fleet entries. No pairs. Only dimensions the source carries are listed in facts: one it lacks (a dimension that needs the gross vehicle mass, engine size or district) would abort, not wait.

supplied.$comment: Sources a maintainer supplies by hand as a CSV, checked and kept in a local store by `python -m pipeline supply <id> <csv>` (pipeline/supplied.py). The Action never runs that command and nothing here is fetched. `fields` maps a logical field name of the top-level `fields` block to the CSV column that carries it; `extra_fields` are public columns the register does not have, kept in the store under the name given; `private_columns` must be in the header and are dropped, so no owner field reaches the store or any output. The store is kept out of git for now (.gitignore): whether it may live in the public repository is the user's decision.

nzta_dashboard.$max_month_change_comment: A month already in the last good build may differ from it by at most this share, unless the ledger records that month as replaced (the dashboard restates past months; a restatement is recorded, not silent).

events.$enum_columns_comment: The columns whose values must come from their enum in the schema table of enum_doc. The values are read from the table; this list makes a row that stops parsing as an enum abort the build instead of dropping its check.

register_archive.$comment: The whole register for each snapshot month, one row per vehicle, kept as one Parquet file in a private store outside git (pipeline/archive.py). It holds every field of pipeline/expected_schema.json except never_pulled: the chassis and engine numbers, which are never asked for. The first 11 characters of the VIN and the owner's postcode are kept in this private file only: neither is bound, built into the cube or published (D-076). The row id is pulled for paging and left out of the file.
register_archive.attribution: Motor Vehicle Register open data, NZ Transport Agency Waka Kotahi, licensed CC BY 4.0. One row per vehicle on the register at the snapshot date.
